root_cause.text: `ieee80211_ml_reconfiguration()` in mac80211 trusted the 4-bit `link_id` parsed from the ML Reconfiguration element without validating it against `IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS`, allowing `link_id == 15` to index past the 15-element `link_removal_timeout[]` stack array and cause an out-of-bounds write.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states `link_id is taken from the ML Reconfiguration element (control & 0x000f), so it can be 0..15` and `link_removal_timeout[] has IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS (15) elements, so index 15 is out-of-bounds`; the patch adds `if (link_id >= IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS) continue;` in `net/mac80211/mlme.c` to prevent the invalid access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip invalid multi-link reconfiguration entries whose link IDs exceed the supported maximum.
intent_record.what: A new bounds check was added in `ieee80211_ml_reconfiguration()`: after extracting `link_id` from `prof->control`, the code now skips the rest of the loop iteration with `continue` if `link_id >= IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS` before using `BIT(link_id)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, invalid or out-of-range link IDs are no longer used to set bits in `removed_links` or processed further, preventing the function from operating on unsupported link indices and avoiding potential undefined behavior or incorrect reconfiguration state.

grouping_result.intent: Skip invalid multi-link reconfiguration entries whose link IDs exceed the supported maximum.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds validation to skip invalid ML reconfiguration entries with out-of-range link IDs, preventing the out-of-bounds write caused by trusting the parsed 4-bit link_id.

candidates.rationale: This extracts the 4-bit link_id from the ML Reconfiguration element without any bounds check, allowing an invalid value such as 15 to later be used as an array index and cause an out-of-bounds write.
This uses the unvalidated link_id in bit operations immediately after parsing it, reflecting the unsafe trust in the field value that ultimately leads to misuse of invalid link IDs.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement extracts the 4-bit link_id from the ML Reconfiguration control field without validating it against IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS, enabling an out-of-bounds index when an invalid value such as 15 is later used.

This statement immediately uses the unvalidated link_id in a bit operation, reflecting the same unsafe trust in the parsed value that can propagate the invalid link_id and contribute to the out-of-bounds write.
